Just as they had done in various other African countries and conflicts, the Soviets supported opposition forces with weapons and training. Moscow also launched a propaganda campaign exaggerating British involvement in the conflict in order to boost support for intervention. The Soviets were large suppliers of munitions and training, but refused to directly enter the conflict. Notebooks taken from political officers attached to insurgent groups, as well as uniforms and weaponry from the Eastern bloc confirmed Russian and Chinese sponsorship and ideology. This was further substantiated by the apprehension of a KGB general by Rhodesian troops during the pre-emptive strike to the ZANLA operated base at "New Farm" at [Chimoio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chimoio "Chimoio"), Mozambique in November 1977.\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] ZAPU’s strategy shifted to plans for conventional warfare in 1977–79, backed by Soviet logistical guidance and Cuban training of 6,000 ZIPRA in batches of 2,000 from 1977 onwards at [Boma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boma,_Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "Boma, Democratic Republic of the Congo") and [Lupea](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lupea&action=edit&redlink=1 "Lupea (page does not exist)") (formerly Vila Luso) in eastern Angola. Concurrently, the ZANU army, based principally in [Mozambique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mozambique "Mozambique"), relied increasingly upon the People’s Republic of China, and Maoist strategies of mobilization and revolutionary warfare. By 1976, Ethiopia, Yugoslavia and Rumania were also offering more training facilities to ZANU. During the war, [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel")'s government declared its support for Rhodesia and cultivated material ties. \[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:NOTRS "Wikipedia:NOTRS")_\] Israel gave Rhodesia the right to produce its own Uzis alongside material shipments. This resulted in the Uzi becoming standard in the Rhodesian army, police, and its white citizens.\[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:NOTRS "Wikipedia:NOTRS")_\] Helicopters provided by Israel to Rhodesia were also used in counter-insurgency operations.\[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:NOTRS "Wikipedia:NOTRS")_\] These counter-insurgency operations were based on Israeli tactics, as Israeli companies were used to construct a 500-mile belt of landmines along the border of Mozambique and Zambia.[\[74\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBeit-Hallahmi198863-82)\[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:NOTRS "Wikipedia:NOTRS")_\] In the United States, a political alliance of segregationists and the nascent [Religious Right](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_right_in_the_United_States "Religious right in the United States") spread propaganda supporting Rhodesia, helped to recruit Americans to join and fight in Rhodesia's military through magazines such as _[Soldier of Fortune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soldier_of_Fortune_/(magazine/) "Soldier of Fortune (magazine)")_, and unsuccessfully lobbied the United States government to officially recognise Rhodesia's sovereignty.[\[75\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-83) ### Civil disobedience (1957–1964) \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rhodesian_Bush_War&action=edit§ion=13 "Edit section: Civil disobedience (1957–1964)")\] [![Image 45: A map. See description](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/Rhodesialand.png/330px-Rhodesialand.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rhodesialand.png) In 1962, Rhodesia was split about equally between black _(orange and purple)_ and white _(yellow)_ areas; however, the population was 95% black and 5% white. The ruling [United Federal Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Federal_Party "United Federal Party") proposed the removal of some racially defined boundaries.[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWindrich197542%E2%80%9345-84) In September 1956, bus fares in [Salisbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harare "Harare") were raised so high that workers were spending 18% to 30% of their earnings on transportation.[\[77\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMuzondidya2005167%E2%80%93170-85) In response, the [City Youth League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Youth_League "City Youth League") boycotted the United Transport Company's buses and succeeded in preventing the price change. On 12 September 1957 members of the Youth League and the defunct ANC formed the [Southern Rhodesia African National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesia_African_National_Congress "Southern Rhodesia African National Congress"), led by Joshua Nkomo. The [Whitehead administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Whitehead "Edgar Whitehead") banned the SRANC in 1959 and arrested 307 leaders, excluding Nkomo who was out of the country, on 29 February in Operation Sunrise.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStearns20021069-31)[\[77\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMuzondidya2005167%E2%80%93170-85)[\[78\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTELake197632-86) Nkomo, Mugabe, [Herbert Chitepo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_Chitepo "Herbert Chitepo"), and [Ndabaningi Sithole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ndabaningi_Sithole "Ndabaningi Sithole") established the National Democratic Party in January 1960. Nkomo became its leader in October. An NDP delegation headed by Nkomo attended the constitutional conference in January 1961. Nkomo initially supported the constitution, but reversed his position after other NDP leaders disagreed. The government banned the NDP in December 1961 and arrested NDP leaders, excluding Nkomo who, again, was out of the country. Nkomo formed the [Zimbabwe African People's Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe_African_People%27s_Union "Zimbabwe African People's Union") which the Whitehead administration banned in September 1962.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStearns20021069-31)[\[77\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMuzondidya2005167%E2%80%93170-85)[\[78\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTELake197632-86) The [United Federal Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Federal_Party "United Federal Party") (UFP) had been in power since 1934, earning it the nickname of "the establishment", and roughly represented Southern Rhodesian commercial and major agricultural interests.[\[79\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWindrich197542-87) The UFP contested the [1962 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesian_general_election,_1962 "Southern Rhodesian general election, 1962") on a ticket of racial "partnership", whereby blacks and whites would work together.[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWindrich197542%E2%80%9345-84)[\[80\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith199746%E2%80%9347-88) All ethnically discriminatory legislation would be immediately repealed, including the Land Apportionment Act, which defined certain areas of the land as eligible for purchase only by blacks, others as exclusively for whites, and others as open for all races.[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWindrich197542%E2%80%9345-84) About 45% of the country was split in this way; another 45% comprised reserved Tribal Trust Lands (TTL), which housed tribesmen, and gave local chiefs and headmen a degree of self-government in a similar manner to American [Indian reservations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_reservation "Indian reservation"). The remainder was national land. The country had originally been split up in this way during the early days of white immigration to prevent the new arrivals from using their superior finances to buy all of the land in the country.[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWindrich197542%E2%80%9345-84) The UFP proposed to repeal the black and white purchase areas, but keep the Tribal Trust and national lands.[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWindrich197542%E2%80%9345-84) It also committed to general black advancement. These proposals proved largely repugnant to the mostly white electorate, which feared that premature black ascendancy would threaten Rhodesia's economic prosperity and security, as well as their own personal affairs.[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWindrich197542%E2%80%9345-84)[\[81\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith199743%E2%80%9347-89) Most turned away from the ruling UFP party, causing it to lose in the 1962 election to the newly formed [Rhodesian Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Front "Rhodesian Front") (RF), a conservative party opposed to any immediate shift to black rule.[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWindrich197542%E2%80%9345-84) [Winston Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Field "Winston Field") and [Ian Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Smith "Ian Smith") became prime minister and Deputy Prime Minister, respectively.[\[82\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith199747-90) Nkomo, legally barred from forming a new party, moved ZAPU's headquarters to [Dar es Salaam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dar_es_Salaam "Dar es Salaam"), Tanzania.[\[78\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTELake197632-86) In July 1963, Nkomo suspended [Ndabaningi Sithole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ndabaningi_Sithole "Ndabaningi Sithole"), [Robert Mugabe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Mugabe "Robert Mugabe"), [Leopold Takawira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leopold_Takawira "Leopold Takawira"), and [Washington Malianga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Malianga "Washington Malianga") for their opposition to his continued leadership of ZAPU.[\[83\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTECaryMitchell1977101-91) On 8 August, they announced the establishment of the [Zimbabwe African National Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe_African_National_Union "Zimbabwe African National Union"). ZANU members formed a militant wing, the [Zimbabwe African National Liberation Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe_African_National_Liberation_Army "Zimbabwe African National Liberation Army"), and sent ZANLA members to the People's Republic of China for training.[\[78\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTELake197632-86) ### First phase (1964–1972) \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rhodesian_Bush_War&action=edit§ion=15 "Edit section: First phase (1964–1972)")\] [![Image 46](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/RhodesiaAllies1965.png/250px-RhodesiaAllies1965.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:RhodesiaAllies1965.png) The geopolitical situation at the time of UDI on 11 November 1965. Rhodesia is coloured green, countries friendly to the nationalists are coloured orange and countries friendly to the government (South Africa and Portugal) are shown in purple. On 4 July 1964, ZANU insurgents ambushed and murdered a white foreman from Silverstreams Wattle Company, Pieter Johan Andries (Andrew) Oberholzer. The killing had a lasting effect on the small, close-knit white community.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBinda200838-21)[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTECilliers19844-22)[\[84\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTERogers199839-92) The Smith administration detained ZANU and ZAPU leaders in August 1964. The major leaders imprisoned were [Ndabaningi Sithole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ndabaningi_Sithole "Ndabaningi Sithole"), [Leopold Takawira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leopold_Takawira "Leopold Takawira"), [Edgar Tekere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Tekere "Edgar Tekere"), [Enos Nkala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enos_Nkala "Enos Nkala") and [Maurice Nyagumbo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Nyagumbo "Maurice Nyagumbo"). The remaining military leaders of the ZANLA Dare ReChimurenga were [Josiah Tongogara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josiah_Tongogara "Josiah Tongogara") and the barrister [Herbert Chitepo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_Chitepo "Herbert Chitepo"). Operating from bases in [Zambia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zambia "Zambia") and later from [Mozambique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mozambique "Mozambique"), militants began launching attacks against Rhodesia.[\[85\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTESt._John20071-93) The conflict intensified after Rhodesia's [Unilateral Declaration of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unilateral_Declaration_of_Independence_/(Rhodesia/) "Unilateral Declaration of Independence (Rhodesia)") (UDI) from Britain on 11 November 1965.[\[84\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTERogers199839-92) [Sanctions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_sanctions "International sanctions") ([embargo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embargo "Embargo")) were imposed by Britain and endorsed by member states of the United Nations. The embargo meant that Rhodesia was hampered by a lack of modern equipment but it used other means to receive vital war supplies such as [oil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petroleum "Petroleum"), munitions, and arms via the [apartheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid "Apartheid") government of South Africa and Portugal. War material was also obtained through elaborate international smuggling schemes through Portuguese Mozambique, domestic production, and captured infiltrating enemy combatants.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith1997109%E2%80%93116-36) Five months later, on 28 April 1966, the Rhodesian Security Forces engaged militants in [Sinoia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinoia "Sinoia"), during the [first major engagement of the war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Sinoia "Battle of Sinoia").[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStearns20021069-31) Seven ZANLA men were killed, and in retaliation the survivors killed two civilians at their farm near Hartley three weeks later.[\[84\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTERogers199839-92) During Portuguese rule of Mozambique, until 1974–1975, Rhodesia was able to defend its border with Zambia relatively easily and prevent many guerrilla incursions. It set up a strong defence along the [Zambezi River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zambezi_River "Zambezi River") running from [Lake Kariba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Kariba "Lake Kariba") to the Mozambique border. Here 30-man camps were established at 8-kilometre intervals supported by mobile rapid reaction units. From 1966 to 1970, these defences accounted for 175 insurgents killed for the loss of 14 defenders.[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-Britannica_1971_259-55) The conflict continued at a low level until 21 December 1972 when ZANLA conducted the [attack on Altena Farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Altena_Farm "Attack on Altena Farm") in north-east Rhodesia. In response, the Rhodesians moved to attack nationalists in their foreign camps and staging areas before they could infiltrate into Rhodesia.[\[86\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTERogers199839%E2%80%9340-94) Secret cross-border operations by the [Special Air Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Special_Air_Service "Rhodesian Special Air Service") began in the mid-1960s, with Rhodesian Security Forces already engaging in [hot pursuits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_pursuit "Hot pursuit") into Mozambique. However, three weeks after the attack on Altena Farm, ZANLA killed two civilians and abducted a third into Mozambique and then Tanzania. In response, SAS troops were inserted into Mozambique with the approval of the Portuguese administration, in the first officially sanctioned external operation. The Rhodesian government began authorising more external operations.[\[86\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTERogers199839%E2%80%9340-94) In the first phase of the conflict (until the end of 1972), Rhodesia's political and military position was strong. Nationalist guerrillas did not make serious inroads. In the early 1970s, the two main nationalist groups faced serious internal divisions, aid from the [Organisation of African Unity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_of_African_Unity "Organisation of African Unity") was temporarily suspended in 1971, and 129 nationalists were expelled from Zambia after they were alleged to have plotted against President [Kenneth Kaunda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Kaunda "Kenneth Kaunda").[\[87\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBritannica1972235-95) Britain's efforts to isolate Rhodesia economically had not produced major compromises by the Smith Government. Indeed, late in 1971 the British and Rhodesian Governments had negotiated a compromise political settlement which would have bowed to the Smith Government's agenda of postponing majority rule into the indefinite future. When it was found that such a delayed approach to majority rule was unacceptable to most of Rhodesia's African population, the deal fell apart.[\[88\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTERyan2004-96) In 1971, Rhodesia joined [Alcora Exercise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcora_Exercise "Alcora Exercise"), a secret defensive alliance for Southern Africa, formalised in 1970 by Portugal and South Africa. Alcora deepened the political and military co-operation between the three countries against the revolutionary insurgency in Rhodesia, Angola, Mozambique and [South West Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_West_Africa "South West Africa") and against the hostile neighbouring countries. However, the end of Portuguese rule in Mozambique created new military and political pressures on the Rhodesian Government to accept the principle of immediate majority rule. ### Second phase (1972–1979) \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rhodesian_Bush_War&action=edit§ion=16 "Edit section: Second phase (1972–1979)")\] For Rhodesian Army counter-insurgency tactics, see [Fireforce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fireforce "Fireforce"). The black nationalists continued to operate from secluded bases in neighbouring [Zambia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zambia "Zambia") and from [FRELIMO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FRELIMO "FRELIMO")\-controlled areas in the Portuguese colony of [Mozambique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mozambique "Mozambique"), making periodic raids into [Rhodesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesia "Rhodesia"). By 1973, guerrilla activity was increasing in the aftermath of the Altena Farm raid, particularly in the northeast part of the country where portions of the African population were evacuated from border areas, and compulsory military service for whites was extended to one year.[\[89\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBritannica1974600-97) As the war intensified, [conscription was raised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conscription_in_Rhodesia "Conscription in Rhodesia") to men between the ages of 38 and 50, though this was modified in 1977. No white male 17-year-olds were allowed to leave the country. In April 1974, the left-wing [Carnation Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnation_Revolution "Carnation Revolution") in Portugal heralded the coming end of colonial rule in Mozambique. A transitional government was formed within months and Mozambique became independent under FRELIMO rule on 25 June 1975. Such events proved beneficial to ZANLA and disastrous for the Rhodesians, adding 1,300 kilometres (800 mi) of hostile border.[\[90\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTERogers199840-98) Indeed, with the demise of the [Portuguese Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Empire "Portuguese Empire"), Ian Smith realised Rhodesia was surrounded on three sides by hostile nations and declared a formal state of emergency. Soon Mozambique closed its border, however Rhodesian forces continued to cross the border in "hot pursuit" raids, attacking the nationalists and their training camps, and engaged in skirmishes with Mozambican security forces.[\[91\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-99) By 1975–1976, it was clear that an indefinite postponement of majority rule, which had been the cornerstone of the Smith Government's strategy since UDI, was no longer viable. Even overt South African support for Rhodesia was waning. South Africa began scaling back economic assistance to Rhodesia, placed limits on the amount of fuel and munitions being supplied to the Rhodesian military, and withdrew the personnel and equipment they had previously provided to aid the war effort, including a border police unit that had been helping guard the Rhodesia-Zambia border.[\[92\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBritannica1976619%E2%80%93620-100) In 1976, the length of active military service was extended to 18 months; this took effect immediately, with soldiers about to end their one-year service finding their active service extended. Even after discharge from regular service, white men entered the reserve forces, and were often called up for duty and subjected to long military service. Rhodesia recruited more black men to volunteer for military service. Although some raised questions about their loyalty, the Rhodesian government stated that it had no doubts about their loyalty, and planned to train black officers. Legislation to conscript blacks was introduced and came in effect in 1979, but the response to call-ups was poor. Rhodesia also recruited foreign volunteers for service, with groups of foreigners who served in Rhodesia including the [Crippled Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Crippled_Eagles "The Crippled Eagles") and [7 Independent Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7_Independent_Company_/(Rhodesia/) "7 Independent Company (Rhodesia)").[\[93\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-fall-101)[\[94\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-102)[\[95\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-103)[\[96\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-104)[\[97\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-105) Late in 1976, Ian Smith accepted the basic elements of the compromise proposals made by US Secretary of State [Henry Kissinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Kissinger "Henry Kissinger") to introduce majority rule within two years.[\[98\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-106) The Smith Government then sought to negotiate an acceptable settlement with moderate black leaders, while retaining strong white influence in key areas. The Rhodesian military, in turn, aimed to erode the rising military strength of the ZANLA and ZIPRA to the greatest extent possible in order to "buy time" for an acceptable political settlement to be reached. #### Use of biological and chemical weapons \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rhodesian_Bush_War&action=edit§ion=17 "Edit section: Use of biological and chemical weapons")\] As the war continued to intensify, the Rhodesian Security Forces initiated a Chemical and Biological Weapons (CBW) programme to kill guerrillas both inside Rhodesia and in external camps in Zambia and Mozambique. The effort had three fronts.[\[99\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTECross2017-107) First, it aimed to eliminate guerrillas operating inside Rhodesia through contaminated supplies either provided by contact men, recovered from hidden caches, or stolen from rural stores.[\[100\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-108) Secondly, it aimed to contaminate water supplies along guerrilla infiltration routes into Rhodesia, forcing the guerrillas to either travel through arid regions to carry more water and less ammunition or travel through areas patrolled by the security forces.[\[101\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-109) Finally, the Rhodesians sought to hit the guerrillas in their camps in Mozambique by poisoning food, beverages, and medicines. The chemicals most used in the Rhodesian programme were [parathion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parathion "Parathion") (an organophosphate insecticide) and [thallium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thallium_poisoning "Thallium poisoning") (a heavy metal commonly found in rodenticide).[\[102\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-110) Biological agents the Rhodesians selected for use also included _Vibrio cholerae_ (causative agent of [cholera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cholera "Cholera")) and _Bacillus anthracis_ (causative agent of [anthrax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthrax "Anthrax")). They also looked at using _Rickettsia prowazekii_ (causative agent of [epidemic typhus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidemic_typhus "Epidemic typhus")), and _Salmonella typhi_ (causative agent of [typhoid fever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoid_fever "Typhoid fever")), and toxins—such as ricin and [botulinum toxin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botulinum_toxin "Botulinum toxin").[\[99\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTECross2017-107) #### Laying of minefields \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rhodesian_Bush_War&action=edit§ion=18 "Edit section: Laying of minefields")\] Between 1976 and 1979, the Rhodesian Army laid extensive minefields along the country's eastern and northern borders to prevent infiltration and resupply of fighters based in Zambia and Mozambique. The mines were laid in dense patterns, one of which was known as the "Cordon Sanitaire"[\[103\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-111) in six main districts and were estimated at independence to cover 511 sq km, later revised down to 310 sq km. The Zimbabwe Government estimated that the minefields contained 2.6 million anti-personnel landmines.[\[104\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-112) The Rhodesian Security Forces called up part-time soldiers on 2 May 1976 in preparation for a major counter-offensive.[\[105\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-113) On 9 August 1976, Rhodesian [Selous Scouts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selous_Scouts "Selous Scouts") aided by former ZANLA commander Morrison Nyathi attacked a ZANLA camp at Nyadzonya in Mozambique containing over 5,000 guerrillas and several hundred refugees. The Selous Scouts, who numbered 72, dressed in FRELIMO uniforms and disguised their vehicles, attaching FRELIMO licence plates and painting them in FRELIMO colours. White soldiers wore black ski masks. They crossed the unmanned border into Mozambique at 0005 hours on 9 August and drove through the early morning to the camp, passing several FRELIMO sentries who saluted them as they went by.[\[106\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTELohmanMacPherson1983chpt._4-114) When they reached the ZANLA camp at 0825 hours the six ZANLA soldiers on duty allowed them to enter, and the Rhodesian vehicles moved in and took up prearranged positions around the edge of the parade ground, on which stood about 4,000 guerrillas. When all was ready a Rhodesian soldier took his vehicle loudspeaker and announced in [Shona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shona_language "Shona language"): "_Zimbabwe tatora_", meaning "we have taken Zimbabwe", and Nyathi blew a whistle signalling the cadres to muster. The cadres began cheering and ran towards the vehicles, packing around them as more ran onto the parade ground from other areas of the camp.[\[106\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTELohmanMacPherson1983chpt._4-114) The Rhodesians then opened fire and continued shooting until there was no movement on the parade ground, then they returned to Rhodesia. More than 300 ZANLA insurgents were reported killed by the Rhodesians, with four Selous Scouts lightly wounded. This figure is corroborated by ZANLA's official report,[\[i\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-115) though publicly both ZANLA and ZIPRA claimed that Nyadzonya had been a refugee camp.[\[106\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTELohmanMacPherson1983chpt._4-114) Later, on 7 October 1976, militants bombed a railroad bridge over Matetsi River when a train carrying ore passed over.[\[107\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-matetsi-116) Black nationalist guerrillas attacked a tea plantation and killed 27 black workers near the Mozambican border on 21 December 1976.[\[108\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-117) #### Escalation of the war (1977) \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rhodesian_Bush_War&action=edit§ion=20 "Edit section: Escalation of the war (1977)")\] [![Image 47](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/2/26/Victims_of_the_Vumba_Massacre%2C_1978.jpg/250px-Victims_of_the_Vumba_Massacre%2C_1978.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Victims_of_the_Vumba_Massacre,_1978.jpg) White civilians; a woman and two young children killed at Elim [Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission_/(Christianity/) "Mission (Christianity)") in eastern Rhodesia by ZANLA guerrillas in the 1978 [Vumba massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vumba_massacre "Vumba massacre").[\[109\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-TimeJuly1978-118)[\[110\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-119) By 1977, the war had spread throughout Rhodesia. ZANLA continued to operate from Mozambique and remained dominant among the Mashona peoples in eastern and central Rhodesia. Meanwhile, ZIPRA remained active in the north and west, using bases in Zambia and Botswana, and were mainly supported by the Ndebele tribes.[\[90\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTERogers199840-98) With this escalation came sophistication, organisation and modern weapons for the guerrillas, and although many were still untrained, an increasing number were trained in Communist bloc and other sympathetic countries.[\[111\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTERogers199840%E2%80%9341-120) [![Image 48](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/Scoutwithgun.jpg/250px-Scoutwithgun.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Scoutwithgun.jpg) A Rhodesian soldier questioning villagers near the border with Botswana in 1977 Weapons fielded included [TT pistols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TT_pistol "TT pistol"), [PPSh-41](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PPSh-41 "PPSh-41") submachine guns, [AK-47](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AK-47 "AK-47") and [AKM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AKM "AKM") assault rifles, [SKS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SKS "SKS") semi-automatic carbines, [RPD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RPD_machine_gun "RPD machine gun") and [RPK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RPK "RPK") light machine guns, as well as [RPG-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RPG-2 "RPG-2") and [RPG-7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RPG-7 "RPG-7") rocket propelled grenade launchers and various Soviet [grenades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenades "Grenades"). The Rhodesians only discovered how well equipped the nationalists had become when raids on guerrilla base areas towards the end of the war revealed mortars, 12.7 mm and 14.5 mm heavy machine guns and even heavier calibre weapons such as 122 mm multiple rocket launchers.[\[112\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTERogers199835-121) On 3 April 1977, General [Peter Walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Walls "Peter Walls") announced that the government would launch a campaign to win the "hearts and minds" of Rhodesia's black citizens.[\[113\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedman2006-122) In May, Walls received reports of [ZANLA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZANLA "ZANLA") forces massing in the city of [Mapai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mapai,_Mozambique "Mapai, Mozambique") in [Gaza Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Province "Gaza Province"), Mozambique. Prime Minister Smith gave Walls permission to destroy the base. Walls told the media the Rhodesian forces were changing tactics from contain and hold to [search and destroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Search_and_destroy "Search and destroy"), "adopting hot pursuit when necessary".\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] On 30 May 1977, during [Operation Aztec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Aztec "Operation Aztec"), 500 troops crossed the Mozambican border and travelled 100 km (60 mi) to Mapai, engaging the [ZANLA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZANLA "ZANLA") forces with air cover from the Rhodesian Air Force and paratroopers in [C-47 Dakotas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-47_Dakotas "C-47 Dakotas"). The Rhodesian government said the military killed 32 ZANLA fighters and lost one Rhodesian pilot. The Mozambican government disputed the number of casualties, saying it shot down three Rhodesian planes and a helicopter and took several thousand troops prisoner, all of which was denied by Minister of Combined Operations, Roger Hawkins.[\[114\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKalley1999224-123)[\[115\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-gamble-124)[\[116\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-tactics-125) [Kurt Waldheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Waldheim "Kurt Waldheim"), the [Secretary-General of the United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary-General_of_the_United_Nations "Secretary-General of the United Nations"), condemned the incident on 1 June, and Walls announced a day later that the Rhodesian military would occupy [Mapai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mapai,_Mozambique "Mapai, Mozambique") until they had eliminated ZANLA's presence. But the American, British, and Soviet governments also condemned the raid[\[114\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKalley1999224-123) and Rhodesian forces later withdrew from the area. The [United Nations Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council "United Nations Security Council") denounced the incursion of the "illegal racist minority regime in Southern Rhodesia" in [Resolution 411](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_411 "United Nations Security Council Resolution 411"), on 30 June 1977.[\[117\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-denouncillegal-126) Militants [bombed a Woolworths department store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salisbury_Woolworths_bombing "Salisbury Woolworths bombing") in [Salisbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harare "Harare") on 6 August 1977, killing 11 and injuring 70.[\[118\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMuzondidya2005246-127) Militants from Mozambique [killed 16 black civilians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Odzanu_Junction_Farm "Attack on Odzanu Junction Farm") in eastern Rhodesia on 21 August, burning the farmworkers' homes on a white-owned farm.[\[119\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-random-128) In November 1977, in response to the buildup of ZANLA guerrillas in Mozambique, Rhodesian forces launched [Operation Dingo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Dingo "Operation Dingo"), a pre-emptive combined arms surprise attack on guerrilla camps at Chimoio and Tembue in Mozambique. The attack was carried out over three days, from 23 to 25 November 1977. These operations reportedly inflicted thousands of casualties on Robert Mugabe's ZANLA cadres, probably blunting guerrilla incursions in the months that followed, but a steady intensification of the insurgency continued through 1978. To disrupt FRELIMO's hold on Mozambique, the Rhodesian [Central Intelligence Organisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Organisation "Central Intelligence Organisation") helped to create and support an insurgency movement within Mozambique. This guerrilla group, known as [RENAMO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RENAMO "RENAMO"), battled with FRELIMO even as Rhodesian forces fought the ZANLA within Mozambique. [![Image 49](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/Rhodesian_Security_Forces_operational_areas.png/330px-Rhodesian_Security_Forces_operational_areas.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rhodesian_Security_Forces_operational_areas.png) Map showing the operational areas of the Rhodesian Security Forces during the conflict. In May 1978, 50 civilians were killed in crossfire between Marxist militants and the Rhodesian military, the most civilians killed in an engagement until then.[\[120\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-crossfire-129) In July, Patriotic Front members killed 39 black civilians and the Rhodesian government killed 106 militants.[\[121\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-civ-130) By mid-1978, black nationalist guerrillas had killed nearly 40 Christian missionaries.[\[109\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-TimeJuly1978-118) Seven white Catholic missionaries were killed by guerrillas at [St. Paul's Mission, Musami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Paul%27s_High_School,_Musami "St. Paul's High School, Musami") on 6 February 1977.[\[122\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-131) In the single worst attack on missionaries, 12 British missionaries and their children were killed in the [Vumba massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vumba_massacre "Vumba massacre") on 23 June 1978.[\[123\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-132) On 4 November 1978, Walls said 2,000 Patriotic Front militants had been persuaded to defect and fight for the [Rhodesian Security Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Army "Rhodesian Army"). In December 1978, a ZANLA unit penetrated the outskirts of Salisbury and fired a volley of rockets and incendiary device rounds into the main oil storage depot. The storage tanks burned for five days, giving off a column of smoke that could be seen 130 km (80 mi) away. Half a million barrels of petroleum product—a quarter of Rhodesia's fuel—was destroyed.[\[124\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-133) [![Image 50](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/LeopardVehicleIWMN.jpg/250px-LeopardVehicleIWMN.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LeopardVehicleIWMN.jpg) A [Leopard APC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leopard_security_vehicle "Leopard security vehicle"), mine-protected vehicle, designed and built in Rhodesia during the late 1970s and based on a Volkswagen engine. This example is displayed in the [Imperial War Museum North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_War_Museum_North "Imperial War Museum North"), Manchester, UK In 1978, 450 ZANLA militants entered from Mozambique and attacked the town of [Umtali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutare "Mutare"). At the time, ZANU said the militants were women, an unusual characteristic, but in 1996 [Joyce Mujuru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joyce_Mujuru "Joyce Mujuru") said the vast majority involved were men and ZANU concocted the story to make Western organisations believe women were involved in the fighting.[\[125\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTELyons2004167-134) In retaliation for these acts, the Rhodesian Air Force bombed guerrilla camps 200 kilometres (125 mi) inside Mozambique, using [Canberra B2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Electric_Canberra "English Electric Canberra") aircraft and [Hawker Hunters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawker_Hunter "Hawker Hunter")—actively, but clandestinely, supported by several of the more capable Canberra B(I)12 aircraft of the [South African Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_African_Air_Force "South African Air Force"). Joint-force bomber raids on guerrilla encampments and assembly areas in Mozambique and Zambia were mounted in 1978, and extensive air reconnaissance and surveillance of guerrilla encampments and logistical build-up was carried out by the [South African Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_African_Air_Force "South African Air Force") on behalf of the RhAF. #### Airliners shot down \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rhodesian_Bush_War&action=edit§ion=21 "Edit section: Airliners shot down")\] Rhodesian external operations extended into Zambia after Nkomo's ZIPRA nationalists shot down two unarmed [Vickers Viscount](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vickers_Viscount "Vickers Viscount") civilian airliners with Soviet-supplied [SA-7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SA-7_Grail "SA-7 Grail") heat-seeking missiles. Encamped beneath the path of ascent towards Salisbury from Kariba Airport, the ZIPRA cadres downed [Air Rhodesia Flight 825](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Rhodesia_Flight_825 "Air Rhodesia Flight 825") on 3 September 1978 and [Air Rhodesia Flight 827](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Rhodesia_Flight_827 "Air Rhodesia Flight 827") on 12 February 1979. In the first incident, eighteen civilians on board survived, and five of these went away to find water. Half an hour later nine ZIPRA fighters arrived, promising help; three of the thirteen survivors hid when they saw them. In the words of _Time_ magazine, the ZIPRA cadres "herded together the ten people at the wreckage, robbed them of their valuables, and finally cut them down with automatic weapons fire". Nkomo claimed responsibility for the attack and spoke of it to the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") in a way Rhodesians considered gloating.[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-viscount1-66) In the second attack all 59 people on board were killed in the crash.[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-viscount2-67) Audio from the [cockpit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cockpit "Cockpit") of [Green Leader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Leader "Green Leader") during [Operation Gatling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Gatling "Operation Gatling") at [Westlands Farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Westlands_Farm&action=edit&redlink=1 "Westlands Farm (page does not exist)"). In retaliation for the shooting down of Flight 825 in September 1978, Rhodesian Air Force Canberra bombers, Hunter fighter-bombers and helicopter gunships attacked the ZIPRA guerrilla base at Westlands farm near Lusaka in October 1978, warning Zambian forces by radio not to interfere.[\[126\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMoorcraftMcLaughlin2008140%E2%80%93143-135) The increased effectiveness of the bombing and follow-up 'air mobile' strikes using [Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-47_Skytrain "C-47 Skytrain")\-dropped parachutists and helicopter 'air cav' techniques had a significant effect on the development of the conflict. As late as September 1979, despite the increased sophistication of guerrilla forces in Mozambique, a raid by Selous Scouts, with artillery and air support, on "New Chimoio" still reportedly resulted in heavy ZANLA casualties.[\[j\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-137) However, a successful raid on the Rhodesian strategic fuel reserves in [Salisbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harare "Harare") also underscored the importance of concluding a negotiated settlement and achieving international recognition before the war expanded further. The larger problem was that by 1979, combined ZIPRA and ZANLA strength inside Rhodesia totalled at least 12,500 guerrillas and it was evident that insurgents were entering the country at a faster rate than the Rhodesian forces could kill or capture; 22,000 ZIPRA and 16,000 ZANLA fighters remained uncommitted outside the country.[\[127\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBeckett2007-136) Joshua Nkomo's ZIPRA forces were preparing their forces in Zambia with the intent of confronting the Rhodesians through a conventional invasion. Whether such an invasion could have been successful in the short term against the well trained Rhodesian army and air force is questionable. However, what was clear was that the insurgency was growing in strength daily and the ability of the security forces to continue to control the entire country was coming under serious challenge.[\[106\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTELohmanMacPherson1983chpt._4-114) By putting the civilian population at risk, ZIPRA and the ZANLA had been particularly effective in creating conditions that accelerated white emigration. This not only seriously undermined the morale of the white population, it was also gradually reducing the availability of trained reserves for the army and the police.\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] The economy was also suffering badly from the war; the Rhodesian GDP consistently declined in the late 1970s.[\[127\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBeckett2007-136) Politically, the Rhodesians were therefore pinning all their hopes on the ["internal" political settlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_Settlement "Internal Settlement") that had been negotiated with moderate black nationalist leaders in 1978 and its ability to achieve external recognition and support. This internal settlement led to the creation of [Zimbabwe-Rhodesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe-Rhodesia "Zimbabwe-Rhodesia") under a new constitution in 1979. Under the agreement of March 1978, the country was renamed [Zimbabwe-Rhodesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe-Rhodesia "Zimbabwe-Rhodesia"), and in the [general election of 24 April 1979](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_Zimbabwe_Rhodesia_general_election "1979 Zimbabwe Rhodesia general election"), Bishop [Abel Muzorewa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abel_Muzorewa "Abel Muzorewa") became the country's first black prime minister. On 1 June 1979, [Josiah Zion Gumede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josiah_Zion_Gumede "Josiah Zion Gumede") became president. The internal settlement left control of the military, police, civil service, and judiciary in white hands, and assured whites about one-third of the seats in parliament. It was essentially a power-sharing arrangement between whites and blacks.[\[128\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-138) The factions led by Nkomo and Mugabe denounced the new government as a puppet of white Rhodesians and fighting continued. The hopes for recognition of the internal settlement, and of Zimbabwe-Rhodesia, by the newly elected [Conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Party_/(UK/) "Conservative Party (UK)") government of [Margaret Thatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Thatcher "Margaret Thatcher") did not materialise after the [latter's election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_United_Kingdom_general_election "1979 United Kingdom general election") in May 1979. Likewise, although the US Senate voted to lift sanctions against Zimbabwe-Rhodesia, the [Carter administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carter_administration "Carter administration") also refused to recognise the internal settlement. Thatcher sympathised with the internal settlement and thought of the ZANLA and ZIPRA leaders as terrorists, but was prepared to support a push for further compromise if it could end the fighting.[\[129\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-139) Britain was also reluctant to recognise the internal settlement for fear of fracturing the unity of the [Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations"). Thus later in 1979, the Thatcher government called a peace conference in London to which all nationalist leaders were invited.[\[130\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTERogers199865-140) [![Image 51](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/19/ZIPRA_battalion.jpg/250px-ZIPRA_battalion.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ZIPRA_battalion.jpg) A New Zealand member of the Commonwealth Monitoring Force supervising a ZIPRA assembly point The outcome of this conference would become known as the [Lancaster House Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancaster_House_Agreement "Lancaster House Agreement"). During the conference, the Zimbabwe-Rhodesian Government accepted a watering down of the 1978 internal settlement while Mugabe and Nkomo agreed to end the war in exchange for new elections in which they could participate. The economic sanctions imposed on Rhodesia were lifted in late 1979, and the country reverted to temporary British rule until elections could be held. Under the Constitution of Zimbabwe-Rhodesia (Amendment) (No. 4) Act 1979 of 11 December 1979, the country formally reverted to its colonial status as Southern Rhodesia. The Zimbabwe-Rhodesian parliament voted itself out of power, and [Lord Soames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Soames,_Baron_Soames "Christopher Soames, Baron Soames") was appointed by the British government to rule the country as Governor-Designate, arriving in Salisbury on 12 December to take over from President Gumede.[\[131\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-141) On 21 December 1979, a cease-fire was announced.[\[130\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTERogers199865-140) An election was scheduled for early 1980. The British Commonwealth deployed an observer force, the Commonwealth Monitoring Force, to the country for the transitional period. Britain contributed 800 soldiers and 300 airmen, along with small contingents of sailors and marines. Australia, [Fiji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiji "Fiji"), [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"), and [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand "New Zealand") also contributed smaller numbers of troops. A nine-man British advance party arrived on 8 December to begin establishing a logistics base, and this was followed by the arrival of the main force shortly after.[\[132\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-britains-smallwars-142)\[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:NOTRS "Wikipedia:NOTRS")_\] The war would end in a military stalemate. However, the political compromise which was reached after combat ceased would work to the advantage of the black nationalists, especially those aligned with [ZANU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZANU "ZANU") leader [Robert Mugabe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Mugabe "Robert Mugabe"). Mugabe himself stated in an interview published in the 28 April 1980 edition of the [New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Times "New York Times") "We did not win a military victory ... We reached a political settlement ... A compromise."[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-k_a_vav-8) During the [election of 1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwean_parliamentary_election,_1980 "Zimbabwean parliamentary election, 1980"), there were accusations of voter intimidation by Mugabe's guerrilla cadres, sections of which were accused of not having assembled in the designated guerrilla assembly points as required under the Lancaster House Agreement, and the international observers as well as Lord Soames were accused of looking the other way. The Rhodesian military may have seriously considered a coup d'état in March 1980.[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBinda2008462%E2%80%93472-59) This alleged coup was to consist of two stages: [Operation Quartz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Quartz "Operation Quartz"), coordinated attacks on guerrilla assembly points within the country, and Operation Hectic, the assassination of Mugabe and his key aides.[\[133\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-143)\[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:NOTRS "Wikipedia:NOTRS")_\] However, even in the context of alleged voter intimidation by ZANLA elements, widespread support for Mugabe from large sections of the black population (in particular from the [Shona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shona_people "Shona people") language group which made up the overwhelming majority of the country's population) could not be seriously disputed. Moreover, the clear absence of any external support for such a coup, and the inevitable conflagration that would have engulfed the country thereafter, scuttled the plan.[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBinda2008462%E2%80%93472-59) The election of early 1980 was won by Mugabe, who became prime minister after [ZANU-PF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe_African_National_Union_-_Patriotic_Front "Zimbabwe African National Union - Patriotic Front") received 63% of the vote. By 16 March 1980, all Commonwealth forces had departed, save for 40 infantry instructors who temporarily stayed behind to train the new nation's army.[\[132\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-britains-smallwars-142) On 18 April 1980, interim British rule ended and the country was internationally recognised as independent. The colony of Southern Rhodesia was formally renamed Zimbabwe, and on 18 April 1982, the government changed the name of the country's capital from Salisbury to [Harare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harare "Harare"). According to Rhodesian government statistics, more than 20,000 people were killed during the second war. From December 1972 to December 1979, 1,120 members of the Rhodesian security forces were killed, along with 10,050 guerrillas who were killed in Rhodesia, and an unknown number in Mozambique and Zambia, 7,790 black civilians, and 468 white civilians.[\[93\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-fall-101) After he assumed power, [Robert Mugabe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Mugabe "Robert Mugabe") acted incrementally to consolidate his power, forming a coalition government with his ZAPU rivals and the white minority. The Rhodesian Army was merged with guerrilla forces to form the [Zimbabwe Defence Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe_Defence_Forces "Zimbabwe Defence Forces"), and the Rhodesian security forces were merged with ZANLA and ZIPRA forces. Joshua Nkomo was given a series of cabinet positions. The South African government recruited white Rhodesian Security Forces personnel in what was designated [Operation Winter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Winter_/(South_Africa/) "Operation Winter (South Africa)") and around 5,000 took this up. However, Mugabe was torn between keeping his coalition stable and pressures to meet the expectations of his followers for social change. Clashes between ZANLA and ZIPRA forces took place in 1980 and 1981. In February 1982, Mugabe fired Nkomo and two other ZAPU ministers from his cabinet, triggering bitter fighting between ZAPU supporters in [Ndebele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ndebele_language "Northern Ndebele language")\-speaking region of the country and the ruling ZANU. Between 1982 and 1985, the military crushed armed resistance from Ndebele groups in [Matabeleland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matabeleland "Matabeleland") and the [Midlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midlands,_Zimbabwe "Midlands, Zimbabwe") in a military crackdown known as _[Gukurahundi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gukurahundi "Gukurahundi")_, a Shona term which translates roughly to mean "the early rain which washes away the chaff before the spring rains". The _Gukurahundi_ campaigns were also known as the Matabeleland Massacres.[\[134\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTENyarota2006134-144) The Zimbabwean military's North Korean-trained [Fifth Brigade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwean_Fifth_Brigade "Zimbabwean Fifth Brigade") was deployed to Matabeleland to crush resistance. German journalist Shari Eppel estimates approximately 20,000 Matabele were murdered in these first years after the war;[\[135\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEppel2008-145) most of those killed were victims of public executions.\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] Violence between ZANLA and ZIPRA continued until 1987. In December 1987, the two groups reached an accord which saw them merge into one party known as [ZANU PF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZANU_PF "ZANU PF"), headed by Mugabe. Mugabe then became President and gained additional powers, as the office of prime minister was abolished.\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] Beyond Zimbabwe's borders, as a result of Rhodesian aid and support for [RENAMO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RENAMO "RENAMO"), the Rhodesian Bush War also helped influence the outbreak of the [Mozambican Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mozambican_Civil_War "Mozambican Civil War"), which lasted from 1977 until 1992 and claimed a million lives.[\[136\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-146) Unlike many post-colonial African conflicts, the Rhodesian Bush War spawned an extensive written military historiography.[\[137\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDoronThomas201981-147) Though the territory at the center of the conflict was known by four different names throughout the time of the war, historiographic works tend to call the country "Rhodesia" or "Zimbabwe". Histories that use the former term often focus on the actions of white soldiers without much account of the conflict's political context, while many works that use the latter term frame the event as a victorious guerrilla liberation war.[\[138\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhite20211%E2%80%932-148) ### Rhodesian narratives \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rhodesian_Bush_War&action=edit§ion=27 "Edit section: Rhodesian narratives")\] Many Rhodesian veterans wrote memoirs about their service after the second Bush War \[_[example needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:AUDIENCE "Wikipedia:AUDIENCE")_\], most of them emanating from soldiers who served in the RLI or Selous Scouts. These works were either self-published, published with vanity presses, or with specialized publishing houses.[\[139\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhite202132%E2%80%9333-149) The memoirs tended to focus more on unit culture and non-military activities such as poaching,[\[140\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhite202151%E2%80%9352-150) or "taming" captured African insurgents into domestic servants.[\[141\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhite202152%E2%80%9353-151) Most of these books were released in Africa; few became commercial successes in the United Kingdom or the United States.[\[142\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhite202150-152) Grouped together with fictional novels about the war, the memoirs are sometimes placed in a genre of "neo-Rhodesian" literature.[\[143\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHoward2021721%E2%80%93722-153) Claims involving use of biological and chemical weapons by Rhodesian forces appeared only in post-war literature.[\[144\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhite202129-154) The first major Rhodesian memoir to be released was Reid-Daly's account of the Selous Scouts, _Selous Scouts Top Secret War_, published by Galago—a publishing house run by [Peter Stiff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Stiff "Peter Stiff")—in 1982. Galago continued to be a major publisher of these works.[\[145\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhite202150%E2%80%9351-155) Publishing of these memoirs accelerated during Zimbabwe's economic decline in the 1990s.[\[146\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhite202144-156) These works increasingly incorporated material from other memoirs and some secondary works, though they generally displayed little knowledge of ZANLA's or ZIPRA's version of events. Many also featured direct and indirect criticism of other soldiers and memoirists.[\[147\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhite202147-157) Some of these disputes led to lawsuits.[\[148\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhite202148-158) [Seizures of white-owned farms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_reform_in_Zimbabwe "Land reform in Zimbabwe") in the 2000s led to a massive growth in the literature.[\[146\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhite202144-156) Revised editions of previous memoirs were also common.[\[149\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhite202146-159) Chris Cocks' _Fireforce_ was re-released by Galago and edited by Stiff. Stiff removed all references to drug use in the new edition, since he wanted to portray the RLI as heroes.[\[150\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhite202151-160) ### Zimbabwean nationalist discourse \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rhodesian_Bush_War&action=edit§ion=28 "Edit section: Zimbabwean nationalist discourse")\] Early literature on nationalist guerrillas in Rhodesia tended to focus on ZANLA and ignore ZIPRA.[\[151\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHelliker_et_al.202170-161) Several autobiographies and memoirs were published by Zimbabwean nationalists in the late 1970s and early 1980s. Masipule Sithole, the younger brother of Ndabaningi, wrote _Zimbabwe: Struggles within the Struggle_, which described conflicts between ZANU and ZAPU with an emphasis on ethnic disagreements. David Martin and Phyllis Johnson published _The Struggle for Zimbabwe_ in 1981, which chronicled the formation and development of nationalist movements. It was printed with a favourable foreword by Mugabe and was wielded by the post-independent Zimbabwean government as evidence of the courage and sacrifices of ZANU and ZANLA, including incorporation into secondary school curriculum.[\[152\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHelliker_et_al.202171%E2%80%9372-162) The first major academic work covering the nationalist guerrilla perspective of the war was Terence Ranger's _Peasant Consciousness and Guerrilla War in Zimbabwe_, published in 1985. It focused on eastern Rhodesia and constituted a largely uncritical account of ZANLA activities in that area. The book did not address violence inflicted by ZANLA on African TTL residents and concluded that rural blacks were "united" in supporting the guerrilla movement. Ranger later reflected that his work duplicated ZANU's nationalist rhetoric.[\[153\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHelliker_et_al.202170%E2%80%9371-163) Romanticised interpretations of the Zimbwabwean nationalist endeavor fell out of scholarly favour in the mid-1990s.[\[154\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHelliker_et_al.202178-164) Since then, more critical works of the nationalist movement have predominated, highlighting complexities in the war.[\[155\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHelliker_et_al.202179-165) More works focusing on ZIPRA have also been published, though the nature of differences between ZANLA and ZIPRA as well as the geographical spread of the two guerrilla forces remains debated.[\[156\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHelliker_et_al.202186-166) In her 1992 book, _Zimbabwe's Guerrilla War_, political scientist Norma J. Kriger rejected "the existing portrait of ZANU's successful politicisation of the Zimbabwean countryside during the liberation war" and concluded that relations between nationalist guerrillas and TTL villagers in Mutoko District were predominantly characterized by violence and coercion.[\[157\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHelliker_et_al.202174%E2%80%9375-167) She also wrote that insofar as peasants voluntarily collaborated with ZANLA, it was often in the hopes of using them to settle petty personal scores and protect their local interests.[\[158\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHelliker_et_al.202175-168) Historian Luise White wrote that the white Rhodesian war accounts did not present a unified and agreed telling of the conflict, and instead "struggled over what being a white Rhodesian meant, and what pasts and futures soldiers brought to the war".[\[159\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhite20213-169) Reflecting on their truthfulness, White stated, "Many of the stories and events in these memoirs are not true, or at least not wholly accurate."[\[148\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhite202148-158) Reid-Daly later testified during a lawsuit involving an authorship dispute that he had "exaggerated or embellished the true story" several times in _Selous Scouts Top Secret War_.[\[160\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Bush_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhite2021116-170) Many of these works maintained that the Rhodesian Army "won every battle but lost at the negotiating 12.content:
[![Image 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f9/Sherman_SSB.jpeg/330px-Sherman_SSB.jpeg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sherman_SSB.jpeg)

A Southern Rhodesian [Sherman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M4_Sherman "M4 Sherman") tank of the [Special Service Battalion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Service_Battalion "Special Service Battalion") during the [Italian Campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Campaign_/(World_War_II/) "Italian Campaign (World War II)")

[Southern Rhodesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesia "Southern Rhodesia"), then a [self-governing colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-governing_colony "Self-governing colony") of the United Kingdom that was located in the now-independent [Zimbabwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe "Zimbabwe"), entered [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") along with Britain shortly after the [invasion of Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Poland "Invasion of Poland") in 1939. By the war's end, 26,121 Southern Rhodesians of all races had served in the armed forces, 8,390 of them overseas, operating in the [European theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_theatre_of_World_War_II "European theatre of World War II"), the [Mediterranean and Middle East theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_and_Middle_East_theatre_of_World_War_II "Mediterranean and Middle East theatre of World War II"), [East Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_African_Campaign_/(World_War_II/) "East African Campaign (World War II)"), [Burma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burma_Campaign "Burma Campaign") and elsewhere. The territory's most important contribution to the war is commonly held to be its contribution to the [Empire Air Training Scheme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Commonwealth_Air_Training_Plan "British Commonwealth Air Training Plan") (EATS), under which 8,235 British, [Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations") and [Allied](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II "Allies of World War II") airmen were trained in Southern Rhodesian flying schools. The colony's operational casualties numbered 916 killed and 483 wounded of all races.

Southern Rhodesia had no diplomatic powers, but largely oversaw its own contributions of manpower and materiel to the war effort, being responsible for its own defence. Rhodesian officers and soldiers were distributed in small groups throughout the British and South African forces in an attempt to prevent high losses. Most of the colony's men served in Britain, East Africa and the Mediterranean, particularly at first; a more broad dispersal occurred from late 1942. Rhodesian servicemen in operational areas were mostly from the country's [white](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_people_in_Zimbabwe "White people in Zimbabwe") minority, with the [Rhodesian African Rifles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_African_Rifles "Rhodesian African Rifles")—made up of black troops and white officers—providing the main exception in Burma from late 1944. Other non-white soldiers and white servicewomen served in East Africa and on the home front within Southern Rhodesia. Tens of thousands of black men were [conscripted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_conscription "Civil conscription") from rural communities for work, first on the aerodromes and later on white-owned farms.

World War II prompted major changes in Southern Rhodesia's financial and military policy, and accelerated the process of industrialisation. The territory's participation in the EATS brought about major economic and infrastructural developments and led to the post-war immigration of many former airmen, contributing to the growth of the white population to over double its pre-war size by 1951. The war remained prominent in the national consciousness for decades afterwards. Since the country's reconstitution as Zimbabwe in 1980, the modern government has removed many references to the World Wars, such as memorial monuments and plaques, from public view, regarding them as unwelcome vestiges of white minority rule and colonialism, despite many Rhodesian servicemen serving in the war being black.

[![Image 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Southern_Rhodesia_in_1939.png/250px-Southern_Rhodesia_in_1939.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Southern_Rhodesia_in_1939.png)

[Southern Rhodesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesia "Southern Rhodesia") in red; other [Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations") territories in pink

When [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") broke out in 1939, the southern African territory of [Southern Rhodesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesia "Southern Rhodesia")[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesia_in_World_War_II#cite_note-2) had been a [self-governing colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-governing_colony "Self-governing colony") of the United Kingdom for 16 years, having gained [responsible government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Responsible_government "Responsible government") in 1923. It was unique in the [British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire") and [Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations") in that it held extensive autonomous powers (including defence, but not foreign affairs) while lacking [dominion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominion "Dominion") status. In practice, it acted as a quasi-dominion, and was treated as such in many ways by the rest of the Commonwealth. Southern Rhodesia's [white](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_people_in_Zimbabwe "White people in Zimbabwe") population in 1939 was 67,000, a minority of about 5%;[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesia_in_World_War_II#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMacDonald1947vii-3) the [black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_people "Black people") population was a little over a million, and there were about 10,000 residents of [coloured](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coloured "Coloured") (mixed) or [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indians_in_Zimbabwe "Indians in Zimbabwe") ethnicity.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesia_in_World_War_II#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWeinrich197315-4) The franchise was non-racial and in theory open to all, contingent on meeting financial and educational qualifications, but in practice very few black citizens were on the electoral roll.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesia_in_World_War_II#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGowlland-Debbas199048%E2%80%9353-5) The colony's [Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Rhodesia "Prime Minister of Rhodesia") was [Godfrey Huggins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godfrey_Huggins,_1st_Viscount_Malvern "Godfrey Huggins, 1st Viscount Malvern"), a physician and veteran of [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I") (1914–18) who had emigrated to Rhodesia from England in 1911 and held office since 1933.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesia_in_World_War_II#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMacDonald1947vii-3)

The [territory's contribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesia_in_World_War_I "Southern Rhodesia in World War I") to the British cause during World War I had been very large in proportion to its white population, though troops had been mostly raised from scratch as there had been no professional standing army beforehand.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesia_in_World_War_II#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGann1965-6) Since the start of self-government in 1923, the colony had organised the all-white [Rhodesia Regiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesia_Regiment "Rhodesia Regiment") into a permanent defence force, complemented locally by the partly paramilitary [British South Africa Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_South_Africa_Police "British South Africa Police") (BSAP). The Rhodesia Regiment comprised about 3,000 men, including reserves, in 1938. The country had fielded black troops during World War I, but since then had retained them only within the BSAP.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesia_in_World_War_II#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGann1965-6) A nucleus of airmen existed in the form of the [Southern Rhodesian Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Air_Force "Rhodesian Air Force") (SRAF), which in August 1939 comprised one squadron of 10 pilots and eight [Hawker Hardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawker_Hart#Hardy "Hawker Hart") aircraft, based at Belvedere Airport near [Salisbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harare "Harare").[\[b\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesia_in_World_War_II#cite_note-8)

The [occupation of Czechoslovakia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_occupation_of_Czechoslovakia "German occupation of Czechoslovakia") by [Nazi Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany") in March 1939 convinced Huggins that war was imminent. Seeking to renew his government's mandate to pass emergency measures, he called an early [election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesian_general_election,_1939 "Southern Rhodesian general election, 1939") in which his [United Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Federal_Party "United Federal Party") won an increased majority. Huggins rearranged his Cabinet on a war footing, making the Minister of Justice [Robert Tredgold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Clarkson_Tredgold "Robert Clarkson Tredgold") Minister of Defence as well.[\[c\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesia_in_World_War_II#cite_note-10) The territory proposed forces not only for internal security but also for the defence of British interests overseas.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesia_in_World_War_II#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMacDonald194710%E2%80%9311-11) Self-contained Rhodesian formations were planned, including a mechanised reconnaissance unit, but Tredgold opposed this. Remembering the catastrophic casualties suffered by units such as the [Royal Newfoundland Regiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Newfoundland_Regiment "Royal Newfoundland Regiment") and the [1st South African Infantry Brigade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Infantry_Brigade_/(South_Africa/) "1st Infantry Brigade (South Africa)") on the [Western Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Front_/(World_War_I/) "Western Front (World War I)") in World War I, he argued that one or two heavy defeats for a white Southern Rhodesian brigade might cause crippling losses and have irrevocable effects on the country as a whole. He proposed to instead concentrate on training white Rhodesians for leadership roles and specialist units, and to disperse the colony's men across the forces in small groups. These ideas met with approval in both Salisbury and London and were adopted.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesia_in_World_War_II#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlake1977233-12)

Southern Rhodesia would be automatically included in any British declaration of war due to its lack of diplomatic powers, but that did not stop the colonial government from attempting to demonstrate its loyalty and legislative independence through supportive parliamentary motions and gestures. The Southern Rhodesian parliament unanimously moved to support Britain in the event of war during a special sitting on 28 August 1939.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rhodesia_in_World_War_II#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWood20059-13)
